title: Static outward rotation against a wall

steps: Lean forwards and support yourself with your good hand on a table.
Let the painful arm hang down loosely.
Gently sway your body so the arm swings forwards and back, then side to side, then in small circles.
Do 15 of each, building to 3 sets of 15.
Ka sunkuya gaba, ka jingina da hannunka mai lafiya a kan tebur.
Ka bar hannun da ke ciwo ya rataya a sake.
A hankali ka girgiza jikinka don hannun ya yi lilo gaba da baya, sannan gefe da gefe, sannan ƙananan da'irori.

Rọra mì ara rẹ kí apá náà lè yí síwájú àti sẹ́yìn, lẹ́yìn náà sí ẹ̀gbẹ́, lẹ́yìn náà ní òbìrí kékeré.

A hankali ka koma farko.

Kee eriri rọba na mkpọchi ọnụ ụzọ n'ọkwa úkwù, jide otu nsọtụ n'aka ọ bụla.
Guzoro ọtọ, dọghachi ikpere aka gị azụ, pịkọta ọkpụkpụ azụ ubu gị ọnụ.

Dúró ṣánṣán kí o fa ìgúnpá rẹ sẹ́yìn, kí o sì fún abẹ́ èjìká rẹ papọ̀.

Sit or stand tall with arms relaxed.

Lower slowly.

Push back to the start.

Ka lanƙwasa gwiwoyin hannunka don ƙirjinka ya kusanci bango, jikinka a miƙe.

Slowly bend forwards and note where your fingertips reach (thighs, knees, shins, floor).
Slowly lean back and side to side. Note any pain and where you feel it.
Record your results weekly.
en.stop: Stop if pain spreads down a leg, or if you feel numbness or weakness.

steps: Tsaya ƙafafunka a buɗe daidai da kugu.
A hankali ka sunkuya gaba ka lura da inda yatsunka suka kai (cinya, gwiwa, ƙwauri, ƙasa).
A hankali ka karkata baya da gefe-gefe. Lura da ciwo da inda kake jin sa.
Rubuta sakamakonka kowane mako.
ha.stop: Ka daina idan ciwo yana bazuwa zuwa ƙafa, ko kana jin dushewa ko rauni.

steps: Guzoro, ụkwụ gị gbasaa dị ka úkwù.
Jiri nwayọ hulata n'ihu, hụ ebe mkpịsị aka gị ruru (apata, ikpere, ọkpụkpụ ụkwụ, ala).
Jiri nwayọ hulata azụ na n'akụkụ abụọ. Hụ mgbu ọ bụla na ebe ị na-enwe ya.
Dee nsonaazụ gị kwa izu.
ig.stop: Kwụsị ma mgbu na-agbada n'otu ụkwụ, ma ọ bụ ị nwere ahụ ịnwụ anwụ ma ọ bụ adịghị ike.

steps: Dúró kí ẹsẹ̀ rẹ jìnnà síra bí ìbàdí.
Rọra tẹ̀ síwájú kí o sì ṣàkíyèsí ibi tí ìka ọwọ́ rẹ dé (itan, orúnkún, ojúgun, ilẹ̀).
Rọra tẹ̀ sẹ́yìn àti sí ẹ̀gbẹ́ méjèèjì. Ṣàkíyèsí ìrora àti ibi tí o ti ń ní i.
Kọ èsì rẹ sílẹ̀ lọ́sọ̀ọ̀sẹ̀.
yo.stop: Dáwọ́ dúró bí ìrora bá ń lọ sí ẹsẹ̀ kan, tàbí bí o bá ní ìkú-ara tàbí àìlágbára.

steps: Stand on one leg holding a worktop for balance.
Rise up onto your toes as high as you can and lower slowly, about one per second.
Count how many full raises you can do before you tire or the height drops.
Do both legs and write down the numbers.
en.stop: Stop if you feel a sudden snap or sharp pain at the back of the heel.

steps: Rest your forearm on a table.
Make a full fist, then spread your fingers wide.
Note whether your fingertips touch your palm and if the fingers straighten fully.
Touch your thumb to each fingertip. Compare both hands weekly.
en.stop: Stop if you get new numbness or the fingers lock.

steps: Sit on a chair.
Try to put on a sock or touch your foot by bending the knee up towards you.
Note if it is easy, possible with effort, or not possible.
Repeat on both sides each week.
en.stop: Stop if you have had a hip replacement and your team told you to avoid bending this far.

steps: Sit on the floor or a bed with legs straight.
Tighten your thigh and check if the back of the knee can touch the bed.
Slide your heel towards you to bend the knee as far as is comfortable. Note the distance from heel to bottom.
Compare both knees and repeat each week.
en.stop: Stop if the knee locks and will not straighten, or swells quickly.

steps: Sit tall in front of a mirror.
Slowly turn your head to look over each shoulder. Note how far you can turn and where it pulls.
Slowly tip your ear to each shoulder, then look down and up.
Score each movement: easy, stiff, or painful. Compare each week.
en.stop: Stop if you feel dizzy, have blurred or double vision, or pain or tingling spreads into your arm.

steps: Zauna a miƙe a gaban madubi.
A hankali ka juya kanka ka kalli kowace kafaɗa. Lura da nisan da za ka iya juyawa da inda yake ja.
A hankali ka karkata kunnenka zuwa kowace kafaɗa, sannan ka kalli ƙasa da sama.
Ba kowane motsi maki: mai sauƙi, mai tauri, ko mai ciwo. Kwatanta kowane mako.
ha.stop: Ka daina idan kana jin jiri, ganinka ya dushe ko ya ninka, ko ciwo ko tsinkewa ya bazu zuwa hannunka.

steps: Nọdụ ala ọtọ n'ihu enyo.
Jiri nwayọ tụgharịa isi gị lee n'elu ubu ọ bụla. Hụ ebe ị nwere ike iru na ebe ọ na-adọ.
Jiri nwayọ hulata ntị gị n'ubu ọ bụla, wee lee ala na elu.
Nye mmegharị ọ bụla akara: mfe, siri ike, ma ọ bụ na-afụ ụfụ. Tụnyere kwa izu.
ig.stop: Kwụsị ma isi na-agba gị gburugburu, anya na-ahụ ihe abụọ ma ọ bụ na-ajọ, ma ọ bụ mgbu na-agbada n'aka gị.

steps: Jókòó ṣánṣán níwájú dígí.
Rọra yí orí rẹ láti wo orí èjìká kọ̀ọ̀kan. Ṣàkíyèsí bí o ti lè yí tó àti ibi tí ó ti ń fà.
Rọra tẹ etí rẹ sí èjìká kọ̀ọ̀kan, lẹ́yìn náà wo ilẹ̀ àti òkè.
Fún ìgbésẹ̀ kọ̀ọ̀kan ní àmì: rọrùn, le, tàbí ń dùn. Fi wé ara wọn lọ́sọ̀ọ̀sẹ̀.
yo.stop: Dáwọ́ dúró bí òòyì bá ń kọ́ ọ, bí ojú rẹ bá ń ríran méjì tàbí ṣókùnkùn, tàbí bí ìrora bá ń lọ sí apá rẹ.

steps: Stand in front of a mirror.
Lift each arm forwards and up as high as you can. Note where it stops or hurts.
Place your hand behind your head, then behind your lower back. Note how far you reach.
Compare left and right, and repeat each week.
en.stop: Stop if the shoulder feels like it slips out, or if you get sudden severe pain.

steps: Stand next to a kitchen worktop or sturdy chair, with your hand just above it.
Lift one foot off the floor and time how long you can stand still, up to 30 seconds.
Do each leg twice and write down your best time for each.
Compare the two sides and repeat every 2 to 4 weeks.
en.stop: Stop and hold on if you feel unsteady. Do not try this alone if you have fallen recently.

steps: Tsaya kusa da teburin kicin ko kujera mai ƙarfi, hannunka kaɗan a samansa.
Ɗaga ƙafa ɗaya daga ƙasa ka auna tsawon lokacin da za ka iya tsayawa cak, har zuwa daƙiƙa 30.
Yi kowace ƙafa sau biyu ka rubuta mafi kyawun lokaci.
Kwatanta ɓangarorin biyu ka maimaita kowane mako 2 zuwa 4.
ha.stop: Ka tsaya ka riƙe idan kana jin rashin daidaito. Kada ka yi kai kaɗai idan ka faɗi kwanan nan.

steps: Guzoro n'akụkụ tebụl kichin ma ọ bụ oche siri ike, aka gị n'elu ya ntakịrị.
Bulie otu ụkwụ n'ala, gụọ ogologo oge ị nwere ike iguzo jụụ, ruo sekọnd 30.
Mee ụkwụ ọ bụla ugboro abụọ, dee oge gị kacha mma.
Tụnyere akụkụ abụọ ahụ, mee ya ọzọ kwa izu 2 ruo 4.
ig.stop: Kwụsị jide ihe ma ị na-ama jijiji. Emela ya naanị gị ma ọ bụrụ na ị dara n'oge na-adịbeghị anya.

steps: Dúró nítòsí ibi ìdáná tàbí àga tó le, kí ọwọ́ rẹ wà lókè rẹ̀ díẹ̀.
Gbé ẹsẹ̀ kan sókè kúrò ní ilẹ̀, kí o sì ka bí o ti lè dúró jẹ́ẹ́ tó, títí dé ìṣẹ́jú-àáyá 30.
Ṣe ẹsẹ̀ kọ̀ọ̀kan lẹ́ẹ̀mejì kí o sì kọ àkókò tó dára jùlọ sílẹ̀.
Fi ẹ̀gbẹ́ méjèèjì wé ara wọn kí o tún un ṣe ní gbogbo ọ̀sẹ̀ 2 sí 4.
yo.stop: Dáwọ́ dúró kí o di nǹkan mú bí o bá ń mì. Má ṣe é ní ìwọ nìkan bí o bá ṣubú láìpẹ́ yìí.

steps: Use a firm chair without wheels, against a wall. Sit in the middle with arms crossed on your chest.
When ready, stand up fully and sit back down as many times as you can in 30 seconds.
Count the full stands. Write down the number and the date.
Repeat every 2 to 4 weeks to see your progress. Your specialist will explain what your number means.
en.stop: Stop if you feel dizzy, chest pain or very short of breath, or if a joint gives way.

steps: Yi amfani da kujera mai ƙarfi marar taya, a jingine da bango. Zauna a tsakiya, hannunka a haɗe a ƙirji.
Idan ka shirya, ka tashi tsaye sosai ka zauna sau nawa za ka iya cikin daƙiƙa 30.
Ƙirga cikakkun tsayuwa. Rubuta adadin da kwanan wata.
Maimaita kowane mako 2 zuwa 4 don ganin ci gabanka. Ƙwararrenka zai bayyana ma'anar adadinka.
ha.stop: Ka daina idan kana jin jiri, ciwon ƙirji, ko numfashi ya yi maka wuya sosai, ko wani gaɓa ya kasa.

steps: Jiri oche siri ike na-enweghị wiil, dabere na mgbidi. Nọdụ n'etiti ya, aka gị gafere n'obi gị.
Mgbe ị dị njikere, bilie kpamkpam ma nọdụ ala ọzọ ugboro ole ị nwere ike n'ime sekọnd 30.
Gụọ ugboro ole i biliri. Dee ọnụọgụ ahụ na ụbọchị ya.
Mee ya ọzọ kwa izu 2 ruo 4 iji hụ ọganihu gị. Ọkachamara gị ga-akọwa ihe ọnụọgụ gị pụtara.
ig.stop: Kwụsị ma isi na-agba gị gburugburu, obi na-afụ gị ụfụ, ume na-akpa gị nke ukwuu, ma ọ bụ nkwonkwo ahụ dara.

steps: Lo àga tó le láìní kẹ̀kẹ́, tí ó fara ti ògiri. Jókòó sí àárín rẹ̀, kí apá rẹ dábùú lórí àyà.
Nígbà tí o bá ṣetán, dìde dáadáa kí o sì jókòó padà ní iye ìgbà tí o bá lè ṣe é láàárín ìṣẹ́jú-àáyá 30.
Ka iye ìgbà tí o dìde. Kọ nọ́ńbà náà àti ọjọ́ sílẹ̀.
Tún un ṣe ní gbogbo ọ̀sẹ̀ 2 sí 4 láti rí ìlọsíwájú rẹ. Onímọ̀ rẹ yóò ṣàlàyé ohun tí nọ́ńbà rẹ túmọ̀ sí.
yo.stop: Dáwọ́ dúró bí òòyì bá ń kọ́ ọ, bí àyà bá ń dùn ọ́, bí èémí bá ń kúrú jù, tàbí bí oríkèé kan bá yẹ̀.

steps: Stand next to a worktop with a hand just above it.
Place one foot directly in front of the other, heel touching toes.
Time how long you can hold this, up to 30 seconds. Then swap feet.
Write down your times.
en.stop: Hold on straight away if you feel unsteady.

steps: Tsaya kusa da teburin kicin, hannunka kaɗan a samansa.
Sa ƙafa ɗaya kai tsaye a gaban ɗayan, diddige yana taɓa yatsu.
Auna tsawon lokacin da za ka iya riƙewa, har zuwa daƙiƙa 30. Sannan ka canza ƙafa.
Rubuta lokutanka.
Guzoro n'akụkụ tebụl kichin, aka gị n'elu ya ntakịrị.
Tinye otu ụkwụ n'ihu nke ọzọ kpọmkwem, ikiri ụkwụ metụ mkpịsị ụkwụ.
Gụọ ogologo oge ị nwere ike ijide ya, ruo sekọnd 30. Wee gbanwee ụkwụ.
Dee oge gị.
Dúró nítòsí ibi ìdáná kí ọwọ́ rẹ wà lókè rẹ̀ díẹ̀.
Gbé ẹsẹ̀ kan sí iwájú èkejì tààrà, kí gìgísẹ̀ kan ìka ẹsẹ̀.
Ka bí o ti lè dì í mú tó, títí dé ìṣẹ́jú-àáyá 30. Lẹ́yìn náà pààrọ̀ ẹsẹ̀.
Kọ àkókò rẹ sílẹ̀.
Place a chair with arms against a wall. Mark a spot 3 metres (about 4 big steps) away.
Sit with your back against the chair. Ask someone to time you.
On 'go', stand up, walk at your normal safe pace to the mark, turn, walk back and sit down.
Write down the time. Use your usual walking aid if you have one.
en.stop: Only do this with another person present. Stop if you feel dizzy or unsteady.

steps: Sa kujera mai hannu a jikin bango. Yi alama a nisan mita 3 (kusan manyan taki huɗu).
Zauna bayanka a jingine da kujera. Ka ce wani ya auna lokaci.
Idan aka ce 'tafi', ka tashi, ka yi tafiya a saurinka na lafiya zuwa alamar, ka juya, ka dawo ka zauna.
Rubuta lokacin. Yi amfani da sandar tafiyarka idan kana da ita.
ha.stop: Ka yi kawai idan akwai wani a wurin. Ka daina idan kana jin jiri ko rashin daidaito.

steps: Tinye oche nwere aka n'akụkụ mgbidi. Kaa akara ebe dị mita 3 (ihe dị ka nnukwu nzọụkwụ anọ).
Nọdụ ala, azụ gị dabere n'oche. Gwa mmadụ ka ọ gụọ oge.
Mgbe ha kwuru 'gaa', bilie, jee ije n'ọsọ gị dị nchebe ruo n'akara ahụ, tụgharịa, laghachi wee nọdụ ala.
Dee oge ahụ. Jiri osisi ije gị ma ọ bụrụ na i nwere.
ig.stop: Mee ya naanị mgbe onye ọzọ nọ. Kwụsị ma isi na-agba gị gburugburu ma ọ bụ ị na-ama jijiji.

steps: Gbé àga onípá sí ògiri. Sàmì sí ibi tó jìnnà ní mítà 3 (bíi ìgbésẹ̀ ńlá mẹ́rin).
Jókòó kí ẹ̀yìn rẹ fara ti àga. Ní kí ẹnìkan ka àkókò fún ọ.
Nígbà tí wọ́n bá sọ 'lọ', dìde, rìn ní ìwọ̀n ìrìn rẹ tó ní ààbò dé àmì náà, yípadà, rìn padà kí o sì jókòó.
Kọ àkókò náà sílẹ̀. Lo ọ̀pá ìrìn rẹ bí o bá ní.
yo.stop: Ṣe é nìkan nígbà tí ẹlòmíràn bá wà níbẹ̀. Dáwọ́ dúró bí òòyì bá ń kọ́ ọ tàbí o bá ń mì.

title: Get up, walk and sit check

steps: Press your palms together in front of your chest with fingers pointing up.
Slowly lower your hands, keeping the palms together, until you feel a stretch. Note the height.
Then put the backs of your hands together, fingers pointing down, and lift slowly.
Compare each week.
en.stop: Stop if you feel sharp pain or tingling in the fingers.

steps: NHS web page with mobility and strengthening exercises for the mid back, each with a video.
Start with mobility exercises and add strengthening as they become comfortable.

title: Mid back pain: NHS exercise page

steps: Stand with your back against a wall, arms bent in a goalpost shape against the wall.
Slide your arms up the wall as far as is comfortable.
Slide them back down, keeping the back and arms near the wall.
Do 15 repetitions, 3 times a day.
Place a tennis ball between your upper back and a wall, beside the spine (not on it).
Lean into it gently and roll slowly up and down.
Pause on tight spots for 20 to 30 seconds.
Use comfortable pressure, once or twice a day.

title: Tennis ball rolling for upper back pain

steps: Start on hands and knees with your back flat.
Slowly reach one arm forwards and the opposite leg back.
Hold, keeping your back still, then return and change sides.
Do 5 to 15 each side, 3 times a day.
NHS leaflet explaining chest wall (musculoskeletal) pain and gentle exercises.
Chest wall pain can feel worrying but is often linked to muscles and joints.
Always get new chest pain checked first by a doctor.

title: Exercises for breast pain caused by the chest wall

steps: Hold onto a door frame with both hands at chest height.
Sit your hips back and let your upper back round, so your shoulder blades spread apart.
Hold 30 seconds while breathing slowly.
Repeat 3 times.
Start with gentle stretches for the area between the shoulder blades.
Follow with shoulder blade squeezes to strengthen the muscles.
Move slowly and keep the shoulders down.
Do 10 repetitions of each strengthening exercise.
Follow the gentle exercises for posture, breathing and trunk strength.
Keep movements slow and comfortable.
Focus on standing and sitting tall without strain.
Do 8 to 10 repetitions of each, once a day.
Lie on your side with knees bent and arms straight out in front together.
Lift the top arm and open it across to the other side, following it with your eyes.
Keep your knees together. Return slowly.
Repeat 20 times each side, 3 times a day.
Lie on your back with a rolled towel across your upper back, under your shoulder blades.
Support your head with your hands.
Gently let your upper back bend back over the towel, then return.
Repeat 20 times, 3 times a day.
Stand side-on to a wall with your feet a small step away.
Turn your upper body towards the wall and place both hands on it.
Let your chest and shoulders turn, keeping your hips facing forwards.
Repeat 20 times, both sides, 3 times a day.

title: Wall rotations for the mid back

steps: Place a rubber band around your fingers and thumb.
Open your hand against the band, then close slowly.
Follow the other finger spreading and thumb exercises in the video.
Do 10 repetitions each, once a day.

title: Top five hand and finger strengthening exercises with rubber bands

steps: Explains carpal tunnel syndrome and why symptoms are often worse at night.
A wrist splint at night can help keep the wrist straight.
Includes gentle exercises and advice about when to seek further help.

source: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Carpal tunnel syndrome: information for patients

steps: Sit with your elbow bent and your hand in front of you.
